title: Input-Shaper Drift After Maintenance
dataSources: Print jobs (`octoprint:job`), printer telemetry (`printer:telemetry`), Klipper resonance metrics (`klipper:telemetry`), resin print logs (`resinprint:job`), tool usage (`tool:usage`), filament inventory (`filament:spool`), and workshop air readings (`workshop:air`).
app: Maker telemetry from OctoPrint, Moonraker, printer firmware sensors, resin printer job logs, smart dryboxes, and workshop tool sensors streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=klipper:telemetry metric="resonance"
| stats earliest(shaper_freq_hz) as baseline_hz latest(shaper_freq_hz) as current_hz by printer axis maintenance_cycle
| eval drift_hz=round(current_hz-baseline_hz,1)
| eval drift_abs=abs(drift_hz)
| sort - drift_abs
description: Compares resonance and input-shaper frequencies before and after maintenance cycles to see when tune quality has drifted.
value: Mechanical changes quietly alter print dynamics, and this view shows when a printer should be re-calibrated instead of blaming the slicer.
implementation: Capture resonance test results each time belts, rails, or toolheads are serviced and record the maintenance cycle identifier.
visualization: Table of baseline and current shaper frequencies by printer axis.
grandmaExplanation: It logs whether the printer's vibration tuning has shifted after repairs or upgrades, which can hurt print quality until you recalibrate it.
